blocks.prompt: 7 (i) A bag contains 8 red balls, 7 green balls. Find the total number of possible ways in which five balls are selected in a way: 3 red and 2 green.
blocks.explanation:
Five balls are chosen: 3 from the 8 red and 2 from the 7 green. The order of picking does not matter.
We must count the selections.
Plan: \({}^{8}C_{3} \times {}^{7}C_{2}\).
steps:
Given: 8 red, 7 green; choose 3 red and 2 green (\(3 + 2 = 5\) balls).
To find: the number of ways.
Method: Each colour is a combination; both choices are made together, so multiply (fundamental principle of counting).

Choose the red balls
\[{}^{8}C_{3} = \dfrac{8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1} = 56\]
Why: 3 red balls out of 8, order not important.

Choose the green balls
\[{}^{7}C_{2} = \dfrac{7 \cdot 6}{2 \cdot 1} = 21\]
Why: 2 green balls out of 7.

Multiply
\[56 \times 21 = 1176\]
Why: Every red choice can be paired with every green choice.

Check
\[1176 \div 21 = 56 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Dividing back gives the red count, so the product is right.

blocks.prompt: 7 (ii) A bag contains 8 red balls, 7 green balls. Find the total number of possible ways in which five balls are selected in a way: 1 red and 4 green.
blocks.explanation:
Five balls are chosen: 1 from the 8 red and 4 from the 7 green. The order of picking does not matter.
We must count the selections.
Plan: \({}^{8}C_{1} \times {}^{7}C_{4}\).
steps:
Given: 8 red, 7 green; choose 1 red and 4 green (\(1 + 4 = 5\) balls).
To find: the number of ways.
Method: Each colour is a combination; both choices are made together, so multiply (fundamental principle of counting).

Choose the red balls
\[{}^{8}C_{1} = \dfrac{8}{1} = 8\]
Why: 1 red balls out of 8, order not important.

Choose the green balls
\[{}^{7}C_{4} = {}^{7}C_{3} = \dfrac{7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1} = 35\]
Why: 4 green balls out of 7. We used \({}^{7}C_{4} = {}^{7}C_{3}\): choosing 4 to take is choosing 3 to leave.

Multiply
\[8 \times 35 = 280\]
Why: Every red choice can be paired with every green choice.

Check
\[280 \div 35 = 8 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Dividing back gives the red count, so the product is right.

blocks.prompt: 7 (iii) A bag contains 8 red balls, 7 green balls. Find the total number of possible ways in which five balls are selected in a way: 4 red and 1 green.
blocks.explanation:
Five balls are chosen: 4 from the 8 red and 1 from the 7 green. The order of picking does not matter.
We must count the selections.
Plan: \({}^{8}C_{4} \times {}^{7}C_{1}\).
steps:
Given: 8 red, 7 green; choose 4 red and 1 green (\(4 + 1 = 5\) balls).
To find: the number of ways.
Method: Each colour is a combination; both choices are made together, so multiply (fundamental principle of counting).

Choose the red balls
\[{}^{8}C_{4} = \dfrac{8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5}{4 \cdot 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1} = 70\]
Why: 4 red balls out of 8, order not important.

Choose the green balls
\[{}^{7}C_{1} = \dfrac{7}{1} = 7\]
Why: 1 green balls out of 7.

Multiply
\[70 \times 7 = 490\]
Why: Every red choice can be paired with every green choice.

Check
\[490 \div 7 = 70 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Dividing back gives the red count, so the product is right.

blocks.prompt: 7 (iv) A bag contains 8 red balls, 7 green balls. Find the total number of possible ways in which five balls are selected in a way: All the red balls.
blocks.explanation:
All 5 balls must be red, so no green ball is taken.
We must count the ways to choose 5 red balls out of 8.
Plan: \({}^{8}C_{5} \times {}^{7}C_{0}\), and \({}^{7}C_{0} = 1\).
steps:
Given: 8 red, 7 green; all 5 chosen balls are red.
To find: the number of ways.
Method: Choose 5 of the 8 red balls; the green part is "choose 0 of 7", which can happen in only 1 way.

Choose 5 red balls
\[{}^{8}C_{5} = {}^{8}C_{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1} = 56\]
Why: \({}^{n}C_{r} = {}^{n}C_{n-r}\) makes the work shorter (3 factors instead of 5).

Green balls
\[{}^{7}C_{0} = 1\]
\[56 \times 1 = 56\]
Why: Corollary \({}^{n}C_{0} = 1\): taking no green ball can be done in only one way.

Check
\[{}^{8}C_{5} = \dfrac{8!}{5!\,3!} = \dfrac{40320}{120 \times 6} = 56 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The full formula gives the same value.
